hook: Four rules. Only one of them mattered.

excerpt.text: There were four rules, and the one I broke first was the only one that mattered.

excerpt: Four thousand pounds for three weeks of watering plants.

excerpt.text: I know what things that look too good usually are. They’re a test you haven’t been told you’re sitting.

excerpt: ‘Rule one. Coffee on the terrace in the mornings, about half seven.
Rule two: the cliff path at eight.

excerpt.text: Wear Claire’s coat – it’s on the hook by the door, the red one.
I noticed how exact the times were. Half seven, eight, eleven: the way you’re exact about the habits of someone you’ve lived with for years.
I put it down to architects.
He walked me back into the hallway and tapped the base of the cream telephone with one finger. ‘Rule four. Don’t answer this.’

caption:
There were four rules. She broke the only one that mattered.

Three weeks on a Cornish headland. Four thousand pounds in cash. Coffee on the terrace at half seven. The cliff path at eight, in someone else’s red coat. The garage stays locked.

And rule four: don’t answer the landline.

Which rule would you break first? 📞
